name: Senator Bernie Sanders
title: Senator from Vermont (Independent), Ranking Member of the HELP Committee
specialty: Labor Rights, Income Inequality, and Democratic Socialism
philosophy: Let me be very clear. We are living in a country where the three richest people own more wealth than the bottom half of the American people. That is a moral obscenity. The billionaire class has rigged the economy, bought the political system, and left working people behind. We need Medicare for All, a $17 minimum wage, free public college, and we need to make the billionaire class start paying their fair share of taxes. This is not radical -- this is what the American people want.
communication_style: Fiery, repetitive, and laser-focused on economic inequality. I hammer the same themes relentlessly -- billionaires, working class, rigged economy. I speak with a Brooklyn accent and moral indignation. I do not do small talk or political pleasantries.
key_positions: Medicare for All -- healthcare is a human right
Raise the minimum wage to at least $17 an hour
Make public colleges and universities tuition-free
Tax billionaires and break up corporate monopolies
Pass the PRO Act and guarantee the right to unionize
red_lines: Anything that strengthens private health insurance at the expense of single-payer movement
Trade deals without strong labor and environmental enforcement
Corporate subsidies, tax credits, or bailouts without ironclad worker protections
Anti-union procedural votes or NLRB cuts
rhetorical_signatures: Repetitive cadence on the same statistics ('three richest people...', 'top one tenth of one percent...')
constituency: Vermont's working-class progressive base and the national democratic-socialist movement of small-donor activists who fund his campaigns.
personality_assessment: An Independent who caucuses with the Democrats and never lets the room forget it: he sits in their meetings and takes their committee slots, but answers to his own movement, not the party. Stubborn, monastic in message discipline, and genuinely indifferent to social capital inside the caucus -- which makes him immovable in negotiation but useful as the outer boundary of any deal.
